newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Weaker Belgian OLOs to remain focused on Paris.
newsitem.headline: Weaker Belgian OLOs to remain focused on Paris.

text.p: Belgian government bonds (OLOs) and futures felt the pinch from a surprise lead by the Left in Sunday's first round of French parliamentary elections and would likely remain squeezed until the second round, dealers said.

Paper was sold here on Monday as elsewhere in Europe on fears that a new left-wing government in Paris might throw up blocks to Europe's economic and monetary union, which could force markets to unwind convergence trades, they said.
"Direction is coming from Paris...Bunds (futures) are some 20 basis points lower, you can add another 10 for OLOs (futures)," a trader said. Volumes were low, though, he added.
Frontmonth OLO futures were down 24 basis points at 120.41 at 0925 GMT, but off an early low at 120.32 hit in a kneejerk reaction to the news from France FR-POL.

"This week will remain quiet, we will be waiting for the second round (next Sunday), people will not be taking positions," the trader said. "If there is confirmation (of the Left's lead), next week could be lively."

Some traders said that with today's Spring Bank holiday in Britain and the U.S. closed for Memorial Day a more pronounced selloff might be seen on Tuesday. Others noted markets were already recovering from the early offloading of paper.

The Belgian franc saw some mild pressure in line with the French franc, which, dealers said, was keeping Belgian money market rates relatively high. Some said the National Bank was squeezing liquidity to help the currency.
The other feature today was the auction of OLO 26 (6.25 pct March 2007) and 27 (4.00 pct Jan 2000) coupled with the maturing of OLO 15 (6.75 percent May 1997).

One trader said 73 billion francs worth of OLO 15 was still outstanding and expected about half of that to be ploughed back into OLO 26 -- the current 10-year benchmark -- and OLO 27. Sixty or 70 percent of that would end up in Belgian hands.
"The auction could be worth 35 to 40 billion, which would be reasonable, the Treasury would be happy with that...on a day when the foreigners (the U.K. and the U.S.) are not taking part," he added.
He noted the paper would go straight into portfolios, thus doing little for market volume.
Another trader said the expiry might tempt the Treasury BELA to hold prices on the auction stock low so as to draw as much cash as possible out of the market to help it finance the redemption.
